learning_outcomes.description: Synthesise a significant digital solution to an identified problem in the world, overcoming challenges associated with implementing new designs and technologies leading to a clearly documented design proposal.

Apply and consolidate previous experience and skills in human-centred design and software development to develop representations of the design concept at different levels of fidelity in order to better communicate with stakeholders and to clarify and inform project requirements.

Apply sound project management methods and techniques to improve the outcomes of software design projects, where the relative merits of the methods are critiqued and adapted for the project context, making use of relevant tools for strategic planning and scheduling where appropriate
Communicate effectively with stakeholders to gather requirements and understand the problem context, and to manage expectations over the course of a project.

Demonstrate an ability to work successfully in a multi-disciplinary team, and reflectively apply methods and techniques for effective collaborative teamwork, including digital tools and platforms, resolving conflicts where they arise.
Examine and question ethical and professional issues associated with technology projects or products, and apply ethical thinking to your own work.

assessments.task_description:
The primary focus of this Studio course is a team-based project in which students identify a problem, investigate the problem context, and develop a documented design that can be used by another team to implement a working prototype in DECO3801/7381.

Project assessment consists of a sequence of design checkpoints throughout the semester, including Problem Identification, Interim Project Critique, and the Final Exhibit and Documentation. Each checkpoint includes an in-class presentation and the submission of project documentation, with the documentation progressively developed into the project's final design/requirements document.

Feedback provided during the early checkpoints is formative and intended to support students in refining their work. The final project grade is determined holistically, considering the quality of the final outcome together with the design process demonstrated throughout the semester. Detailed assessment requirements and submission instructions are provided in the assessment briefs on Blackboard.

Use of Generative AI

This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI will provide only limited support and guidance. Failure to acknowledge AI/MT use or demonstrate authorship and understanding of the submission may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct and may result in penalties of up to the total marks available for the assessment. Detailed guidance is provided in the assessment brief and on Blackboard.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Presentations and the project exhibit will be in person during scheduled studio sessions. Project documents will be submitted via Turnitin on Blackboard.

assessments.task_description:
The Portfolio is the major individual assessment for Studio 3 and provides the primary evidence of your learning, individual contribution, and professional development throughout the semester.

Your portfolio should present a curated selection of work that demonstrates your contribution to the team project, your design process, and your learning. It should include critical reflection on your decisions, challenges, and outcomes, rather than simply showcasing completed work.

The Portfolio will be assessed on the quality and coherence of the submission, evidence of your individual contribution, the depth of reflection, and the authenticity of the work presented.

Throughout the semester, you will complete individual Exit Slips to support reflection on your progress and contribution. Exit Slips provide formative feedback and contribute to the evidence used to assess your portfolio and individual engagement. Detailed requirements, submission instructions, and expectations for the Portfolio and Exit Slips are provided in the assessment brief on Blackboard.
